+      skipped+=("$name")
+    elif [[ "$name" == fa-* ]]; then
+      refused+=("$name")
+    else
+      uploadable+=("$asset")
+    fi
+  done
+  if [ "${#refused[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
+    echo "::error::release $tag is PUBLISHED — attaching unattached fa-* asset(s) [${refused[*]}] would invalidate its signed SHA256SUMS (gh-2042 AC1: a published release is immutable for fa-* assets). Remediate by re-running the release-provenance job for the tag (it re-hashes the current assets and re-signs), or target the next-version DRAFT instead." >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  for name in "${skipped[@]:-}"; do
+    [ -n "$name" ] || continue
+    echo "✅ gate: $name already on the published release $tag — immutable skip (gh-2042)"
+  done
+  for asset in "${uploadable[@]:-}"; do
+    [ -n "$asset" ] || continue
+    gh release upload "$tag" "$asset" --clobber --repo "$repo"

+  done
+  exit 0
+fi
+

+  exit 0
+fi
+
+echo "::error::unparseable release state for $tag — refusing to attach (gh-2042 fail-closed)" >&2
+exit 1

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Release drift check (gh-2042, AC2): re-download every `fa-*` asset of a
+# release and diff sha256 against the signed SHA256SUMS.
+#
+# The v1.0.680 incident: assets were re-attached to the published release
+# ~2-3h AFTER the manifest was signed, so the manifest no longer described
+# the shipped bytes and every `fa update` / install.sh provenance check on
+# the train failed. This is the CI-side twin of bin/self_manage.dart's
+# verifyReleaseProvenance — same manifest, same digest comparison — run
+# after every release publish and on a schedule
+# (.github/workflows/release-drift-watch.yml). Drift = red run + a details
+# file the remediation step pages from + an auto re-request of
+# release-provenance. Drift must page, not linger.
+#
+# Checks (any hit = drift, exit 1):
+#   - SHA256SUMS / SHA256SUMS.sig present on the release (no signature = no
+#     provenance at all — the SEC-07 #795 fail-closed class);
+#   - every manifest entry's digest matches the downloaded bytes
+#     (sha256sum -c);
+#   - the manifest covers EXACTLY the release's fa-* set (an fa-* asset on
+#     the release that the manifest does not list is a stale manifest — the
+#     v1.0.680 `-mac.zip` shape; a manifest entry the release no longer
+#     serves is a missing asset — the gh-1832 shape).

+# Usage: release_drift_check.sh <tag>
+# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN,
+#      FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR (tests only: verify a pre-populated directory
+#      instead of downloading), FA_DRIFT_DETAILS (drift details file, the
+#      remediation step pages from it; default drift-details.txt in the CWD).

+

+repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
+details="${FA_DRIFT_DETAILS:-drift-details.txt}"
+
+drift=()
+report() { # report <line>: collects the drift finding + names it in the details file
+  drift+=("$1")
+  printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$details"
+}

+workdir="${FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR:-$(mktemp -d)}"
+if [ -z "${FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR:-}" ]; then
+  mkdir -p "$workdir"

+  # match them, and BOTH must be on the release for provenance to exist.
+  gh release download "$tag" --repo "$repo" --dir "$workdir" --pattern 'fa-*'

+fi

+rm -f "$details"

+    report "SHA256SUMS.sig is NOT on release $tag — an unsigned manifest is not provenance"
+  fi

+      case "$line" in
+        *FAILED*|*failed*)

+      esac
+    done < "$workdir/sha-check.log"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Release drift remediation (gh-2042, AC2): when the drift check finds a
+# published release whose assets no longer match the signed SHA256SUMS, this
+# step (a) auto re-requests the release-provenance job for the tag — the job
+# re-hashes the CURRENT assets and re-signs the manifest, which is also the
+# AC3 v1.0.680 remediation mechanism — and (b) pages a DEDUPLICATED issue so
+# drift never lingers silently.
+#
+# The re-request targets the SIGN JOB (`gh run rerun --job`), never the
+# whole tag run: a full rerun would rebuild + re-attach every asset, which
+# the immutability gate (scripts/release_asset_gate.sh, gh-2042 AC1) now
+# refuses on a published release — and a rebuild is not what remediation
+# needs anyway (the shipped bytes are the truth; only the manifest is stale).
+#
+# Paging FIRST-CLASS: the issue is filed even when the re-request fails or
+# the tag run cannot be found (deleted history, PR-only branch names) — the
+# only total failure of this step is the issue filing itself failing.
+#
+# Issue dedup: exact title `[release-drift] SHA256SUMS drift on <tag>` —
+# an open match gets a comment (a fresh data point), never a duplicate.
+#
+# Usage: release_drift_remediate.sh <tag> <drift-details-file>
+# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+tag="${1:?usage: release_drift_remediate.sh <tag> <drift-details-file>}"
+details_file="${2:?usage: release_drift_remediate.sh <tag> <drift-details-file>}"
+repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
+
+details="(drift details unavailable)"
+[ -f "$details_file" ] && details=$(cat "$details_file")
+
+rerun_status="(re-request not possible: no completed workflow run found for tag $tag on ci.yml)"
+# `// 0` (not `// ""`): jq encodes the empty STRING as `""` — with quotes —
+# which would defeat the emptiness guard. 0 is never a real run id.
+run_id=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml --branch "$tag" \
+  --limit 30 --json databaseId,conclusion \
+  --jq '[.[] | select(.conclusion != null)] | first | .databaseId // 0' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+if [ "$run_id" != "0" ] && [ -n "$run_id" ]; then
+  job_id=$(gh api "repos/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id/jobs" --paginate \
+    --jq '.jobs[] | select(.name == "Sign release checksums") | .id' 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)
+  if [ -n "${job_id:-}" ]; then
+    if gh run rerun "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --job "$job_id" 2>/dev/null; then
+      rerun_status="release-provenance re-requested: run $run_id, job $job_id (it re-hashes the current assets and re-signs — gh-2042 AC2/AC3)"
+    else
+      rerun_status="re-request FAILED: gh run rerun $run_id --job $job_id was rejected — rerun the 'Sign release checksums' job manually"
+    fi
+  else
+    rerun_status="re-request FAILED: no 'Sign release checksums' job on run $run_id — rerun release-provenance for the tag manually"
+  fi
+fi
+
+title="[release-drift] SHA256SUMS drift on $tag"
+body="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/release-drift-body.XXXXXX")"
+trap 'rm -f "$body"' EXIT
+{
+  echo "## $title"
+  echo
+  echo "$details"
+  echo
+  echo "**Auto-remediation (gh-2042 AC2):** $rerun_status"
+  echo
+  echo "If the drift persists after the re-run, an attach path replaced fa-* assets on the published release again — find it and gate it (scripts/release_asset_gate.sh). Until the manifest matches the shipped bytes, \`fa update\` / install.sh provenance verification fails for this train."
+} > "$body"
+
+# Dedup: exact open-title match (the inject-failure verify pattern) →
+# comment; otherwise create. Best-effort label so the issues are filterable.
+existing=$(gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --limit 200 \
+  --json number,title --jq '.[] | select(.title == $t) | .number' --arg t "$title" 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)

+  gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body" >/dev/null \
+    || { echo "::error::drift on $tag: could not comment the open drift issue #$existing — page the release owner manually" >&2; exit 1; }
+  echo "✅ drift issue updated: #$existing (dedup — no duplicate filed)"
+else
+  gh label create release-drift --repo "$repo" --color D97706 --description "Published release assets drifted from the signed SHA256SUMS" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+  gh issue create --repo "$repo" --title "$title" --label release-drift \
+    --body-file "$body" >/dev/null \
+    || { echo "::error::drift on $tag: could not file the drift issue — page the release owner manually" >&2; exit 1; }
+  echo "✅ drift issue filed for $tag — paged (gh-2042 AC2: drift must not linger)"
+fi

+# gh-2042 — release drift watch (AC2 + the AC3 remediation vehicle).
+#
+# The v1.0.680 incident: assets were re-attached to the ALREADY-PUBLISHED
+# release ~2-3h after the signed SHA256SUMS was attached; the manifest never
+# re-ran and every `fa update` provenance check on the train failed for
+# macOS-arm64. The attach paths are now gated
+# (scripts/release_asset_gate.sh, gh-2042 AC1) — this workflow is the
+# detection backstop for ANY drift that still reaches a published release:
+#
+#   - after every release publish (the `release: published` event fires when
+#     release-provenance flips the draft — the manifest is on board by then):
+#     verify the tag's shipped bytes against its signed SHA256SUMS;
+#   - on a DAILY schedule: the same check for the latest published release
+#     (the one `fa update` serves) — drift must page, not linger;
+#   - on demand (workflow_dispatch with a tag): the manual remediation
+#     vehicle — dispatching it for v1.0.680 IS the AC3 remediation: the
+#     check detects the stale manifest and the remediation step auto
+#     re-requests the release-provenance job, which re-hashes the CURRENT
+#     assets and re-signs.
+#
+# On drift the run goes red, a deduplicated issue pages the owner, and the
+# "Sign release checksums" job of the tag's ci.yml run is re-requested
+# (scripts/release_drift_remediate.sh — job-scoped rerun, never a full run:
+# a full rerun would rebuild + re-attach, which the AC1 gate refuses on a
+# published release).
+name: Release drift watch
+
+on:
+  release:
+    types: [published]
+  schedule:
+    # Daily, offset from the other crons (ci 23 */2, daily-publish 17 5,
+    # nightly 17 3 / 17 7).
+    - cron: '51 6 * * *'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      tag:
+        description: 'Tag to verify (empty = the latest published release). Dispatch for a stale-manifest tag IS the provenance re-sign remediation (gh-2042 AC3).'
+        required: false
+        type: string
+        default: ''
+
+# SEC-08: explicit minimal default — the job declares its own block below.
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+concurrency:
+  group: release-drift-watch
+  cancel-in-progress: false # a drift check is never preempted mid-page
+
+jobs:
+  drift-watch:
+    name: Verify assets match the signed SHA256SUMS
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 15
+    permissions:
+      contents: read # download the release assets
+      actions: write # re-request the release-provenance job on drift
+      issues: write # the deduplicated drift page

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Attach assets to <tag>'s release, creating it when missing — the single
# draft-capable create path for build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# (issue #282 E3 + review of #294).
#
# Race-idempotent (E3): if `gh release create` loses the view→create race
# (another job/run created the release in between), fall back to
# uploading into the winner's release instead of failing. A failed create
# would fire the job's draft lifecycle guard against the WINNER's
# in-flight draft.
#
# Ownership-stamped: the create path makes a DRAFT (gh-1801 rework: the
# release never goes live from a leg — the tag-run release-provenance job
# publishes + flags latest once the signed SHA256SUMS is attached). The
# body stamps
#   <!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job_id> -->
# and release_draft_guard.sh deletes that draft ONLY on an exact
# run+job match — never the sibling leg's mid-upload draft (daily-publish
# runs the mobile and macOS legs concurrently on the same derived tag).
# The marker is an invisible HTML comment in the body.
#
# Usage: release_attach_or_create.sh <tag> <asset> [<asset>...]
#   reads the release body from release-notes.md in the CWD (a minimal
#   body is written when the file is missing/empty)
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_attach_or_create.sh <tag> <assets...>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
shift
assets=("$@")
if [ "${#assets[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  # gh-1801 hard refusal: creating a release with zero resolved assets is
  # the `fa update` breaker (an empty `latest` 404s every
  # fa-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz until backfill — v1.0.630, 2026-10-23). Attaching
  # is the caller's only honest option when it resolved nothing — fail
  # loud here, never create empty. Pinned by
  # test/release_empty_latest_guard_test.dart.
  echo "::error::no assets to attach for $tag — refusing to create or touch a release with an empty asset list (gh-1801): resolve at least one artifact or skip the release step" >&2
  exit 1
fi

upload_all() { # exists-path: gate-guarded attach + (servable DRAFT-only) publish + latest
  # gh-2042 (AC1): every upload passes the immutability gate — on a
  # PUBLISHED release an unattached fa-* asset refuses the whole call loud,
  # an already-attached one skips, and non-fa store/DMG refreshers keep
  # their clobber-refresh contract. Drafts attach exactly as before.
  for asset in "${assets[@]}"; do
    bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_asset_gate.sh" "$tag" "$asset"
  done
  # Latest policy (#282 + gh-1801 rework + gh-2042): publish + latest ONLY
  # when the release can actually serve `fa update` — that means the signed
  # checksums are already on it (`fa update` hard-fails without
  # SHA256SUMS(.sig), bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate) — AND it is
  # still a DRAFT (the provenance-flip recovery window). A PUBLISHED
  # release is never re-flaged `--latest` here: on an older release that
  # would drag the latest badge (and `fa update`) backwards to a downgrade.
  if release_serves_fa_update; then
    case "$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft 2>/dev/null || echo false)" in
      true)
        gh release edit "$tag" --draft=false --latest --repo "$repo"
        # gh-1899: same duplicate-tag race as the tag train — a twin draft
        # minted by a sibling leg of THIS run would otherwise rot until the
        # 24h sweeper. The tag is published and servable here (the flip is
        # gated on the signed checksums), so own-run twin drafts are orphans.
        bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_draft_dedupe.sh" "$tag" \
          || echo "::warning::gh-1899 twin-draft dedupe failed — the release is published and servable, so this is cleanup noise only; the 24h sweeper remains the backstop"
        ;;
      *)
        echo "release $tag is already published — publish/latest flip skipped (gh-2042: latest never moves backwards; the signed SHA256SUMS re-upload is release-provenance's job)"
        ;;
    esac
  else
    echo "release $tag is not yet servable (no SHA256SUMS on it) — publish+latest left to the release-provenance step (gh-1801)"
  fi
}

# fa-update servability = the signed checksums are on the release. Every
# fa-* archive alone is NOT enough: `fa update` fetches SHA256SUMS(.sig)
# and aborts when either is missing (bin/self_manage.dart).
release_serves_fa_update() {
  local names
  names=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json assets --jq '.assets[].name' 2>/dev/null || true)
  printf '%s\n' "$names" | grep -qE '^SHA256SUMS(\.sig)?$'
}

if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  upload_all
  echo "✅ attached ${#assets[@]} asset(s) to existing release $tag"
  exit 0
fi

# Body: prepared notes (CHANGELOG section / conventional-commit fallback)
# plus the ownership marker the guard verifies before deleting.
notes="release-notes.md"
marker="<!-- release-draft-owner: run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)} -->"
[ -s "$notes" ] || printf 'Release %s — see the CHANGELOG.\n' "$tag" > "$notes"
grep -qF "$marker" "$notes" || printf '\n%s\n' "$marker" >> "$notes"

# A `gh release create` for a MISSING tag mints a lightweight API tag:
# no push event → no ci.yml tag run → no publish/binaries (the v0.1.408
# silent class, issue #597). If the ref is absent, mint it as an
# ANNOTATED tag and push it with the PAT the job already carries
# (GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT in build-macos) so the tag CI fires. The mint
# itself (GH_TOKEN guard, persisted-checkout-extraheader strip, push,
# train-start verification) lives in scripts/release_tag_mint.sh —
# gh-2026: the v1.0.663 / v1.0.665 minted pushes rode actions/checkout's
# persisted GITHUB_TOKEN extraheader (it outranks the URL credentials),
# GitHub suppresses workflow triggers for GITHUB_TOKEN pushes, no tag run
# ever existed on those refs, and the drafts rotted behind green legs.
# A mint whose train does not start now fails loud BEFORE any draft is
# created, so the leg goes red and the failure-path draft guard has
# nothing to reclaim.
# Gate on the DEFINITE missing verdict (ls-remote --exit-code rc 2):
# sandboxes without an origin remote fatal with 128 — indeterminable
# falls through to the plain create path (test fixtures rely on it).
set +e
git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1
ls_remote_rc=$?
set -e
if [ "$ls_remote_rc" -eq 2 ]; then
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_tag_mint.sh" "$tag"
fi

# Bare vX.Y.Z title (#282): matches the tag, matches pub.dev. gh-1801
# rework: the create is DRAFT-ONLY. Whatever this leg resolved
# (AAB/IPA/store APKs, DMGs/zips) is not the signed provenance `fa update`
# demands — a leg that arrives first must never publish the release, let
# alone flag it latest (threads 2/6). The draft is ownership-stamped (the
# marker below) so this job's draft lifecycle guard reclaims it on
# failure; the tag-run binaries job attaches the CLI assets into it and
# release-provenance (ci.yml) publishes + flags latest once SHA256SUMS.sig
# is on board.
if gh release create "$tag" \
  --repo "$repo" \
  --title "$tag" \
  --draft \
  --notes-file "$notes" \
  "${assets[@]}"; then
  echo "✅ created draft release $tag with ${#assets[@]} asset(s) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"
  exit 0
fi

# E3 idempotency: the create may have lost the view→create race — the
# winner's release now exists. Attach instead of failing (a failing
# create would fire the guard against the winner's in-flight draft).
if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  upload_all
  echo "✅ lost the create race — attached ${#assets[@]} asset(s) to the concurrently created release $tag"
  exit 0
fi

echo "::error::release create for $tag failed and no concurrent release appeared — see the step log above" >&2
exit 1

auto_release.sh
pin_release.sh
release_asset_gate.sh
release_attach_or_create.sh
release_dedupe_check.sh
release_dedupe_selftest.sh
release_draft_dedupe.sh
release_draft_guard.sh
release_drift_check.sh
release_drift_remediate.sh
release_lazy_draft.sh
release_notes.sh
release_required_assets.txt
release_tag_mint.sh
stamp_staged_release.sh
verify_pubdev_release.sh

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Lazy DRAFT create for the release train's asset-upload steps (gh-1801).
#
# The train workflows (ci.yml binaries/web-spa, build-macos.yml
# build-macos-cli/build-extension) need a release object to attach assets
# to, but the release must never go live from an upload step: `fa update`
# resolves the `latest` release and hard-fails without the SIGNED
# SHA256SUMS(.sig) (bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate), which only the
# tag-run release-provenance job can upload. This script creates the
# release as a DRAFT — nothing else:
#
#   - body = scripts/release_notes.sh output (curated `## <version>`
#     CHANGELOG section → curated `## Unreleased` → conventional commits;
#     the gh-1172 curated-notes contract), with a minimal fallback —
#     never `--generate-notes` (review threads 3/7);
#   - body carries `<!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job> -->`
#     so scripts/release_draft_guard.sh can reclaim the draft on failure
#     (review threads 4/8) — matrix legs override the identity via
#     RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (e.g. binaries-linux-x64) so a failed leg's
#     guard can never match a sibling's in-flight draft;
#   - the view→create race is tolerated (`|| true`): a sibling leg or the
#     attach path may create the release between our view and create —
#     the loser just uploads into the winner's release;
#   - it NEVER publishes and NEVER flags latest: the single publish point
#     of a tag train is release-provenance's "Upload provenance assets"
#     step (`gh release edit --draft=false --latest` after SHA256SUMS.sig
#     lands). A red provenance leaves the previous release as latest —
#     safe degradation, never a provenance-less latest (v1.0.630 window).
#
# Usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (optional leg-suffixed override),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
identity="${RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY:-run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}}"

# The guard greps exactly this class — validate here so a malformed
# override fails loud instead of stamping a marker the guard could never
# match (a forever-orphaned draft).
printf '%s' "$identity" | grep -Eq '^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' || {
  echo "::error::RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY '$identity' does not match 'run/<id>/job/<name>' — the draft lifecycle guard could never reclaim such a draft" >&2
  exit 1
}

# Already created (by a sibling leg, the attach path, or a previous run)?
# Drafts and published releases both resolve here — upload-only is safe.
if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "release $tag already exists — lazy draft create skipped"
  exit 0
fi

# Body: curated notes (CHANGELOG section / Unreleased / conventional
# commits) plus the ownership marker the guard verifies before deleting.
# stderr is NOT swallowed: release_notes.sh's ::error gates (e.g. the
# duplicate-'## Unreleased' curation guard) must stay visible even when
# the minimal fallback below keeps the train moving.
notes_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/release-lazy-notes.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$notes_file"' EXIT
if ! bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_notes.sh" "$tag" >"$notes_file" ||
  [ ! -s "$notes_file" ]; then
  printf 'Release %s — see the CHANGELOG.\n' "$tag" >"$notes_file"
fi
marker="<!-- release-draft-owner: $identity -->"
grep -qF "$marker" "$notes_file" || printf '\n%s\n' "$marker" >>"$notes_file"

# gh-2026: a `gh release create` for a MISSING ref REST-mints a
# lightweight API tag with NO push event — the v0.1.408 silent class
# (issue #597). The fast legs (build-macos.yml build-extension /
# build-macos-cli) can reach this create before the attach legs
# (release-macos / release-mobile): the silent mint wins the race, every
# attach leg then finds the tag existing and skips the CI-firing
# annotated push, no tag train ever runs, and the draft is stranded
# (swept a day later — the v1.0.663 / v1.0.665 shape). When the ref is
# DEFINITELY missing, mint it through the CI-firing annotated push and
# verify the train started BEFORE creating the draft (dispatch-time call
# sites export GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT for exactly this; the ci.yml tag-run
# call sites always see the tag of their own push event and never enter
# the mint). An indeterminable verdict (no origin remote, rc 128 —
# sandboxed fixtures) falls through to the plain create path.
set +e
git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1
ls_remote_rc=$?
set -e
if [ "$ls_remote_rc" -eq 2 ]; then
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_tag_mint.sh" "$tag"
fi

# DRAFT-first (gh-1801): a create here must never publish — the resolved
# asset list at this point can never include the signed checksums. The
# race-lost create is tolerated (the winner owns the release).
gh release create "$tag" \
  --repo "$repo" \
  --title "$tag" \
  --draft \
  --notes-file "$notes_file" || true
echo "✅ lazy draft ready for $tag (owner $identity) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"

uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          path: dmgs
          pattern: Fa-macos-*
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: List downloaded artifacts
        run: ls -laR dmgs/

      - name: Merge macOS auto-update manifest
        run: |
          python3 -m pip install --user pyyaml
          chmod +x scripts/merge-mac-update-manifest.sh
          scripts/merge-mac-update-manifest.sh dmgs dmgs/latest-mac.yml
          cat dmgs/latest-mac.yml

      - name: Create or update GitHub Release
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # PAT (not the job token) so the tag push fires tag CI — the
          # attach-or-create script builds its push URL only when GH_TOKEN
          # is set; without it `git push ""` died with "fatal: bad
          # repository ''" (2026-10-22 v1.0.626 mobile leg).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          DMGS=$(ls dmgs/*.dmg 2>/dev/null || true)
          ZIPS=$(ls dmgs/*-mac.zip 2>/dev/null || true)
          MANIFEST="dmgs/latest-mac.yml"
          echo "DMGs to upload: $DMGS"
          echo "ZIPs to upload: $ZIPS"

          STABLE_COPIES=()
          for zip in $ZIPS; do
            base=$(basename "$zip")
            # Skip no-sandbox zips from the auto-update stable names; the
            # sandboxed build is the default update feed.
            if [[ "$base" == *nosandbox* ]]; then
              continue
            fi
            if [[ "$base" == *arm64* ]]; then
              cp "$zip" "dmgs/fa-macos-arm64-mac.zip"
              STABLE_COPIES+=("dmgs/fa-macos-arm64-mac.zip")
            elif [[ "$base" == *x86_64* ]]; then
              cp "$zip" "dmgs/fa-macos-x64-mac.zip"
              STABLE_COPIES+=("dmgs/fa-macos-x64-mac.zip")
            fi
          done

          # Extract the raw binary from the .app bundle and upload it as the
          # plain asset name (fa-macos-arm64 / fa-macos-x64) so `fa update`
          # and direct downloads work without knowing the version suffix.
          for zip in $ZIPS; do
            base=$(basename "$zip")
            if [[ "$base" == *nosandbox* ]]; then
              continue
            fi
            unzip -qo "$zip" -d /tmp/fa-extract >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            BIN="/tmp/fa-extract/Fa.app/Contents/MacOS/Fa"
            if [ -f "$BIN" ]; then
              if [[ "$base" == *arm64* ]]; then
                cp "$BIN" "dmgs/fa-macos-arm64"
                ASSETS+=("dmgs/fa-macos-arm64")
              elif [[ "$base" == *x86_64* ]]; then
                cp "$BIN" "dmgs/fa-macos-x64"
                ASSETS+=("dmgs/fa-macos-x64")
              fi
              chmod +x "dmgs/fa-macos-arm64" "dmgs/fa-macos-x64" 2>/dev/null || true

content.text:
4430:    name: Sign release checksums
    name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa, build-extension]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
      # key against the PEM embedded in site/install.sh — that file must be
      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Collect release assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p provenance
          gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --dir provenance --pattern 'fa-*'
          ls -l provenance

      # gh-1832: PUBLISH-BLOCKING required-assets gate. The single source of
      # truth is scripts/release_required_assets.txt, consumed by
      # scripts/assert_release_assets.sh. v1.0.635 published without
      # fa-extension.zip because the extension's only producer (the daily
      # build-macos.yml build-extension leg) attached it to a "latest+1"
      # draft while this train published the tagged release — every leg
      # green, nothing asserted the published set. A missing asset here
      # fails the release run loudly and leaves the release a DRAFT (the
      # previous release stays latest) instead of publishing a partial one.
      - name: Assert required release assets (gh-1832 gate)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

      - name: Build and sign SHA256SUMS
        env:
          FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          cd provenance
          sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS
          if [ -z "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY is not set — refusing to publish a release without signed checksums (SEC-07 #795, fail-closed). Set the repo secret with the release-signing private key."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # The key never outlives the step — trap covers mid-step failure.
          trap 'rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"' EXIT
          openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -out SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          # Self-check: the signature must verify against OUR OWN public key
          # before anything is uploaded.
          openssl rsa -in "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -pubout -out pub.pem 2>/dev/null
          openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # gh-814 r2 trust-anchor drift gate (fail-closed): the public key
          # derived from the secret must equal the PEM embedded in
          # site/install.sh — otherwise every pinned installer would ship an
          # anchor that rejects this release's signed checksums.
          sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/site/install.sh" |
            sed "1s/^.*BEGIN/-----BEGIN/; \$s/END.*\$/END PUBLIC KEY-----/" > embedded-anchor.pem
          openssl pkey -pubin -in embedded-anchor.pem -noout ||
            { echo "::error::site/install.sh trust anchor does not parse as a public key — regenerate installers (dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart)"; exit 1; }
          cmp embedded-anchor.pem pub.pem ||
            { echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY drifted from the trust anchor embedded in site/install.sh — rotate the keypair: update install.signing_public_key in site/install-config.yaml, regenerate installers, and update the repo secret TOGETHER. Refusing to sign (fail-closed)."; exit 1; }
          rm -f pub.pem embedded-anchor.pem

      - name: Upload provenance assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
            provenance/SHA256SUMS provenance/SHA256SUMS.sig \
            --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          # gh-1801 (rework): THE publish point of the train. The release
          # now carries every fa-* asset AND the signed SHA256SUMS(.sig) —
          # the first moment `fa update` can actually serve it (it
          # hard-fails without the signed checksums, bin/self_manage.dart).
          # Flip draft=false + latest here and ONLY here: a red provenance
          # leaves the previous release as latest (safe degradation)
          # instead of stranding a provenance-less one (the v1.0.630
          # empty/partial-latest window class).
          gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --latest --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

      # gh-1899: the flip above publishes exactly ONE release object, but
      # GitHub does not atomically enforce one release per tag — two train
      # legs racing the lazy draft create can BOTH succeed (v1.0.641, run
      # 40163369302: twin drafts 87 ms apart), and the unpicked twin then
      # rots until the 24h sweeper deletes it and files a recurring sweep
      # issue. The tag is published and servable now: reclaim this run's
      # twin drafts. Success-path only — a red provenance keeps the draft
      # as the rerun --failed recovery vessel.
      # Best-effort by design (gh-1899 review): the flip above already
      # published the release — a cleanup-only API blip here must NOT fail
      # the provenance job (release-asset-smoke gates on its result and
      # would silently skip for a release that is actually fine). Warn
      # and stay green; the 24h sweeper remains the backstop.
      - name: Reclaim orphaned draft twins (gh-1899)
        if: success()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_dedupe.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" || echo "::warning::gh-1899 twin-draft dedupe failed — the 24h sweeper remains the backstop"

  # gh-1832 AC3: post-publish smoke. Probes (1) EVERY releases/(latest/)?
  # download/ URL the fa1.dev landing page exposes (site/index.html) and
  # (2) the full required set from scripts/release_required_assets.txt via
  # a 1-byte ranged GET each — red on anything but HTTP 200/206. Rides the
  # tag train only (PR runs never probe release URLs); a 404 here is the
  # owner-facing v1.0.635 symptom caught the same hour it appears.
  release-asset-smoke:
    name: Release asset smoke (landing links + required set)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: release-provenance
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.release-provenance.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||

Chain:

- That job's "Upload provenance assets" step ends with an unconditional `gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --latest` (ci.yml:4515).
- `gh release edit --latest` = "Explicitly mark the release as 'Latest'" (https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_release_edit) — it designates that release as Latest regardless of whether a newer one exists; reruns execute with the original run's ref (GITHUB_REF_NAME = the old tag).

if [ "$is_draft" = "true" ] || [ "$is_latest" = "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" ]; then
 gh release edit --draft=false --latest
else
 gh release edit --draft=false  # no --latest
fi
``

arguments.content:
🚨 **BLOCKING: the AC3 remediation vehicle re-flags an old release `--latest` — a fleet-wide `fa update` downgrade**

The remediation chain this PR wires up can move the `latest` badge **backwards**, which the PR itself declares must never happen:

1. `scripts/release_drift_remediate.sh:43` re-requests the tag's **"Sign release checksums"** job:
   ```bash
   gh run rerun "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --job "$job_id"
   ```
2. That job's "Upload provenance assets" step ends with an **unconditional** flip (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:4515`):
   ```bash
   gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --latest --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
   ```
   A job rerun re-executes **all** its steps with the original run's ref, so `GITHUB_REF_NAME` is the (possibly old) tag.
3. `gh release edit --latest` is "**Explicitly mark the release as 'Latest'**" (https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_release_edit) — it designates that release as Latest *regardless of whether a newer release exists*.
4. The new workflow explicitly advertises the dangerous path as its primary use (`.github/workflows/release-drift-watch.yml:16`): *"dispatching it for v1.0.680 IS the AC3 remediation"*. Once any newer release exists, dispatching drift-watch for an older drifted tag re-flags that older release as Latest → every `fa update` client "updates" **down** to it (the re-signed manifest makes the downgrade pass provenance verification).

The PR's own invariant text: *"A PUBLISHED release is never re-flaged `--latest` here: on an older release that would drag the latest badge (and `fa update`) backwards to a downgrade"* (`scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh:57-58`, same wording in `test/release_publish_imutability_test.dart:10`). The attach path enforces it; the remediation path reintroduces it.

Note the scheduled/`release: published` paths are safe (they only ever target the current latest), so this bites exactly the documented manual-remediation flow.

**Suggested fix** — make the flip conditional in the provenance job (keeps the gh-1801 publish point and the AC4 pin intact):

```bash
is_draft=$(gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft)
is_latest=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ "$is_draft" = "true" ] || [ "$is_latest" = "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" ]; then
  gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --latest --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
else
  # Re-sign remediation of a non-latest tag: publish state is already
  # correct — never drag the latest badge backwards (gh-2042).
  gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
fi
```

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: committed test-run residue files (`release-notes.md`, `drift-details.txt`)**

Both new root files are artifacts of running the new scripts with **fixture** values — `v1.2.3`, `run/111/job/binaries-linux-arm64` and `fa-windows-x64.zip` exist only in the test fixtures:

- `release-notes.md` — the minimal fallback body + draft-owner marker written by `release_attach_or_create.sh` when invoked from the repo root (the current-run marker would be appended on top of the stale one).
- `drift-details.txt` — the drift check's default `FA_DRIFT_DETAILS` output, containing fake findings ("digest drift: fa-windows-x64.zip: FAILED open or read").

This is verifiably residue, not intentional fixtures: running the PR's own verify command regenerates `drift-details.txt` **byte-identical** at the repo root (verified during this review — the tracked file changes on every `dart test` run).

Functional hazard beyond hygiene: the drift-watch workflow pages from `drift-details.txt` in the checkout root. `release_drift_check.sh` only resets that file (`rm -f "$details"`) **after** the downloads, so if the check dies early (e.g. a transient `gh release download` failure — the `fa-*` download at line 47 has no `|| true`), the "Page + auto re-request" step files a GitHub issue quoting this stale committed content as if it were today's drift — a false incident page with fabricated data.

**Fix**: delete both files from the branch and add `drift-details.txt` / `release-notes.md` to `.gitignore` (both are CWD artifacts of the release scripts — nothing on `main` tracks them today).

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: untrusted `${{ }}` interpolation into `run:` shell — use env indirection**

The "Resolve target release" step interpolates `${{ inputs.tag }}` and `${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}` directly into a `run:` block:

```yaml
if [ -n "${{ inputs.tag }}" ]; then
  tag="${{ inputs.tag }}"
```

and the resolved value is then re-interpolated in the two downstream `run:` steps as `"${{ steps.target.outputs.tag }}"`. This is the classic GitHub Actions script-injection pattern: a tag value containing shell metacharacters (`` ` ``, `$( )`, `;`) executes in the runner — a job holding `contents: read` + `actions: write` + `issues: write`.

Both `workflow_dispatch` and release publishing currently require repo write access, so this is not an external-attacker path — but it is exactly the hazard class this repo's SEC-08 posture (explicit least-privilege blocks in this very workflow) works to avoid, and GitHub's security-hardening guide calls for env-var indirection for *all* untrusted template values.

**Fix**:

```yaml
- name: Resolve target release
  id: target
  env:
    DISPATCH_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
    RELEASE_EVENT_TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
  run: |
    set -euo pipefail
    if [ -n "$DISPATCH_TAG" ]; then
      tag="$DISPATCH_TAG"
    elif [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "release" ]; then
      tag="$RELEASE_EVENT_TAG"
    ...
```

and pass the result into the check/remediate steps the same way (`env: TAG: ${{ steps.target.outputs.tag }}` → `"$TAG"`). Repo precedent exists both ways (`release-appstore.yml` interpolates inputs directly — equally flaggable), so this is hardening-for-consistency, not a regression unique to this PR.

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: per-asset gate loop defeats the documented all-or-nothing contract**

The gate's header promises: *"Verdicts (per call, all-or-nothing — a partial attach would still drift the manifest)"*, and `release_asset_gate_test.dart` pins it ("published release + mixed list → refuse ALL, nothing uploaded"). But this caller invokes the gate **once per asset**:

```bash
for asset in "${assets[@]}"; do
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_asset_gate.sh" "$tag" "$asset"
done
```

so the atomicity the gate documents and the tests pin is never exercised in production:

- With assets `[a.zip, fa-bad.tar.gz]` on a PUBLISHED release, the first gate call clobbers `a.zip` before the second call refuses `fa-bad.tar.gz` — a partial mutation the single-call contract forbids (benign for the manifest only because the partial case is non-fa, i.e. by accident of ordering, not by construction).
- Each iteration re-runs `gh release view` (N extra API round-trips per attach) and widens the draft→published TOCTOU window: assets are judged against N different state snapshots.

**Fix** — one call for the whole list (the gate already loops internally and refuses before any upload):

```bash
bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_asset_gate.sh" "$tag" "${assets[@]}"
```

💡 **SUGGESTION: transient download blips are indistinguishable from real drift — they page false incidents**

Two asymmetric error paths conflate "API blip" with "drift":

- Line 48: `gh release download --pattern 'SHA256SUMS*' || true` — a transport-level failure (502, rate limit) is swallowed and reported as *"SHA256SUMS is NOT on release"* → red run + issue page + a pointless release-provenance re-request for a release whose provenance is actually intact.
- Line 47: the `fa-*` download has **no** `|| true` — a transient failure aborts via `set -e` *before* the `rm -f "$details"` reset, so the remediation pages with `(drift details unavailable)` (or stale checkout content) under the **same dedup title** as real drift, polluting the thread a genuine incident relies on.

Both end in a human page, and the check re-runs daily — one runner blip = one page. Since the intent is "drift must page, not linger", consider distinguishing 404 from transport errors: retry once, or capture stderr and only treat an explicit `not found` as the missing-asset verdict while letting other failures fail the step *without* filing the drift issue (an infra error is not drift evidence).

💡 **SUGGESTION: unquoted expansion in the set-diff loops breaks on asset names with spaces**

Lines 74-79 expand `$unlisted` / `$uncovered` unquoted:

```bash
for name in $unlisted; do
```

GitHub release asset names may contain spaces; a name like `fa macos arm64.tar.gz` would (a) never match the `comm` set-diff as a whole line and (b) be reported as several bogus per-word "assets" if it lands in the diff. Read the diffs line-wise instead:

```bash
while IFS= read -r name; do
  [ -n "$name" ] || continue
  report "stale manifest: fa asset $name is on the release but NOT in SHA256SUMS (attached after signing?)"
done <<< "$unlisted"
```

Also worth a one-line note in the header: the check is GNU-bound (`sha256sum`, `find -printf`) — fine for the ubuntu-latest workflow, but it fails confusingly if run locally on macOS.

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST CHANGES

**Summary**: The gh-2042 design (immutability gate + drift watch + auto-remediation) is sound and unusually well-tested (52/52 targeted tests green, `bash -n` clean), but the remediation vehicle can regress `latest` fleet-wide, and two committed test-artifact files pollute the repo root.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 1 BLOCKING: drift remediation re-runs the provenance job, whose unconditional `--draft=false --latest` flip (ci.yml:4515) drags the Latest badge backwards onto an older tag — an `fa update` downgrade
- ⚠️ 4 IMPORTANT: committed test residue (`release-notes.md`, `drift-details.txt` — the latter regenerated byte-identical on every test run); `_runCheck` missing `FA_DRIFT_DETAILS` (root cause of that residue); `${{ inputs.tag }}` interpolated into `run:` shell; per-asset gate loop defeats the documented all-or-nothing contract
- 💡 2 SUGGESTIONS: transient download blips page false drift incidents; unquoted set-diff expansion breaks on asset names with spaces

**Next Steps**:
1. Gate the provenance flip on "still draft OR already latest" (or strip `--latest` when the flip isn't the publish point)
2. Delete `release-notes.md` + `drift-details.txt` from the branch, set `FA_DRIFT_DETAILS` in `_runCheck`, gitignore both artifacts
3. Env-indirect `inputs.tag`; pass the whole asset list to the gate in one call

tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read the contents of a text file or image. Text output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large text files. Images are returned as base64 content. Video files route to a video-capable model when one is available (the bytes are attached or described with attribution); otherwise a note names how to configure video reading.

## Path selectors

Append a trailing selector to `path` to read exactly the lines you need:

- `:N` — start at line N (1-indexed), through end of file. `:N-` is the same.
- `:A-B` — inclusive line range (`:A..B` works too).
- `:A+C` — C lines starting at A.
- `:R1,R2,…` — multiple ranges, sorted and merged (`:5-16,960-973`); blocks are joined with a `…` separator and ranges past end of file are reported as skipped.
- `:raw` — verbatim content: no line numbers, no hashline header, no notices. Combine as `:raw:50-100` or `:50-100:raw`.

Do not combine `offset`/`limit` with a path selector. Selectors only apply to text files (not images).

## Archives

Read inside `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`/`.tgz` files: `archive.zip` lists the root, `archive.zip:dir/` lists a directory, `archive.zip:inner/file.txt` reads a member (selectors apply, e.g. `archive.zip:inner/file.txt:50-60`). Binary members return a note.

## SQLite databases

When the host supports it, `.db`/`.db3`/`.sqlite`/`.sqlite3` paths read as databases: `data.db` lists tables, `data.db:table` shows the schema plus sample rows, `data.db:table:key` fetches one row by primary key (or rowid), `data.db:table?limit=20&offset=40&order=col:desc&where=...` pages a table, and `data.db?q=SELECT ...` runs a raw read-only query.

## Hashline mode

Set hashline=true to prefix lines with line numbers and a [path#TAG] content-hash header for anchoring hashline edit patches (line numbers stay correct on ranged reads). Suppressed by `:raw`.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file, creating parent directories as needed. Overwrites the file if it already exists.

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Edit a file in one of two modes.

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
1:def greet(name):
2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)
4:greet("world")
```

Insert a guard after line 1:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.POST 1:
+    if not name: name = "stranger"
```

Replace line 2 with two lines:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
SWAP 2.=2:
+    greeting = "Hi"
+    msg = f"{greeting}, {name}"
```

Delete line 3:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
DEL 3
```

Add a header and trailer:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.HEAD:
+# generated header
INS.TAIL:
+greet("everyone")
```

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:
```
[PLAN.md#A1B2]
INS.POST 2:
+- task
+  - nested task
```
</example>

<anti-patterns>
# WRONG — `-` rows / bare context lines do not exist. The range deletes; the body is only the new content.
SWAP 3.=3:
    msg = "Hello, " + name
-   print(msg)
+   return msg
# RIGHT
SWAP 3.=3:
+   return msg

# WRONG — a pure insertion done as a widened `SWAP`: you want to add one line after 2,
# but you replace 2.=4, retype the keepers, and risk dropping one.
SWAP 2.=4:
+    msg = "Hello, " + name
+    extra = compute(name)
+    print(msg)
# RIGHT — touch nothing you keep; the new line is the whole body.
INS.POST 2:
+    extra = compute(name)
</anti-patterns>

<critical>
If you remember nothing else:
1. RE-GROUND AFTER EVERY EDIT. Every apply mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — take the next edit's numbers from the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`. Stale tag or surprise? STOP, re-`read`.
2. RANGES ARE TIGHT. Cover only lines that change; a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
3. THE BODY IS THE FINAL CONTENT. Every body row starts with `+`; Markdown bullets use `+- item`, not `- item`.
</critical>

tools.name: ls
tools.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the working directory; returns stdout and stderr, truncated to the last 2000 lines or 50KB. Timeouts you set are retried automatically (3 attempts total) as [bash attempt N]; environment-default timeouts fail once with the partial output. For long-running commands (builds, servers, watchers) pass background: true — you get the job id immediately and a notice when it finishes; check progress with bash_job. A foreground command still running when the user sends a message is moved to a background job untouched (never killed). A command still running after 60s is moved to a background job automatically (never restarted); carried timeouts are NOT auto-retried — retry if the completion notice reports a timeout.

tools.name: bash_job
tools.description: Manage background shell jobs (from bash background: true). Actions: "status" lists running + last 20 exited (all: true = every job; id = one), "output" tails a log (id, lines), "stop" kills a running job (id).

tools.name: lsp
tools.description:
Query a language server for diagnostics, navigation, and renames. For Dart/Flutter workspaces the Dart analysis server (`dart language-server`) starts automatically on first use; other servers can be added via `.fah/lsp.json`.

## Ops

- `diagnostics {path}` — analyzer errors/warnings for a file. Returns `OK` when clean.
- `definition {path, line, character}` — where the symbol at the position is defined.
- `references {path, line, character}` — every reference to the symbol at the position.
- `rename {path, line, character, newName}` — rename the symbol at the position workspace-wide. The server's workspace edit is applied atomically, so barrel files and imports update together; per-file edit counts are reported.

`line` and `character` are 1-indexed and default to 1.

## Rules

- Prefer this over `bash dart analyze` for a single file; diagnostics come back scoped and severity-sorted.
- Prefer `rename` over manual search-and-replace for identifiers: the analysis server finds every reference, including exports and imports.
- Positions point at the symbol's first letter. When unsure of the exact column, `read` the line first.
- Definition/references results render as `file:line:col` with the source line; follow up with `read` for more context.
- If no server is configured for a file type, add one to `.fah/lsp.json` (servers map with `command`, `args`, `fileTypes`, `rootMarkers`).

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web and return ranked results with [n] citation markers, titles, URLs, and snippets. Runs a provider chain (DuckDuckGo first, keyed providers when configured) and falls through on failure. Follow up with web_fetch on a result URL to read the full page.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch a web page and return its main content as Markdown: headings, link anchors, lists, and code blocks are preserved, navigation and boilerplate are stripped. Known sites (pub.dev) are rendered via dedicated handlers. Use it to read pages found with web_search.

tools.name: config
tools.description: Inspect and edit the fa configuration — the user file ~/.fah/config.yaml and the project .fah/config.yaml — without a shell (the same core the `fa config` CLI verbs wrap, available on every host). ops: check = validate both files with the real parsers (errors/warnings/notes + a final ok/failed line); path = list the config file locations and whether each exists; get = the effective value of a dotted key (project scope wins where it participates); set = a surgical single-key write that validates the edited file BEFORE writing, so an invalid value persists nothing. Config keys are documented in the fa-self-config skill — never invent one; unknown keys are rejected. A set result names the file, scope, old -> new value, and whether the change applies live or at next boot.

tools.name: memory_add
tools.description:
# `memory_add` policy

## What to store

Store only **durable** facts — things that must survive across sessions:

- project conventions, architecture decisions and their rationale;
- user preferences, habits, environment facts;
- key discoveries that were expensive to learn (non-obvious behaviour,
  gotchas, working configurations).

Do **not** store task progress, transient state, or anything derivable
from the repository itself (file contents, git history, current diffs).

## The supersede rule

Facts age. When a problem is **solved** or a fact **changes**:

1. delete the outdated record (`memory_delete` by id or exact text —
   deletions are tombstoned, so the old text cannot be re-captured);
2. add the new fact as a fresh record.

Never leave temporary difficulties, workarounds, or "currently broken"
notes in memory forever. A memory full of solved problems actively
misleads future sessions. If you used a record to fix something, that
record's job is done — supersede it.

Before adding anything, `memory_search` for an existing record on the
topic: update (delete + add) instead of duplicating.

## Scope discipline

- **project scope** (default) lives in the project's memory directory and
  is **public**: it is committed to git and shared with everyone who
  clones the repository. Never store secrets, credentials, personal data,
  or anything you would not put in a public commit message.
- **user scope** is global and private to the user's machine. Use it for
  cross-project preferences and facts about the user.

## Style

- One fact per record, concise and self-contained (readable without the
  conversation that produced it).
- Add concrete tags (see [tag_taxonomy.md](tag_taxonomy.md)).
- Prefer facts with staying power: "tests run with `--exclude-tags
  integration`" outlives "I am currently fixing the test suite".

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Search long-term memory for relevant facts, preferences, or past decisions. Use proactively before tasks that might benefit from prior context.

tools.name: memory_list
tools.description: List recent long-term memory entries. Useful to review what the agent already knows.

tools.name: memory_delete
tools.description: Delete a stale, wrong, or obsolete entry from long-term memory by id. Prefer deleting over rewriting when the fact no longer holds at all.

tools.name: schedule_message
tools.description: Send a delayed message to an agent mailbox (your own by default) — schedule a follow-up task to check on something later. The message wakes the recipient when it fires; it survives restarts.

tools.name: ask
tools.description:
Ask the user one or more structured questions when you need clarification or a decision during task execution.

<conditions>
- Multiple approaches exist with significantly different tradeoffs the user should weigh
</conditions>

<instruction>
- Use `questions` for multiple related questions instead of asking one at a time
- Use `recommended` (0-based option index or exact option label) to mark the default; the UI badges it as "Recommended"
- Set `multiSelect: true` on a question to allow multiple selections
- Use short option labels; put explanatory tradeoffs in an option's `description` instead of merging them into the label
- Omit `options` when the answer is free-form text
</instruction>

<caution>
- Provide 2-5 concise, distinct options per question
</caution>

<critical>
- **Default to action.** Resolve ambiguity yourself using repo conventions, existing patterns, and reasonable defaults. Exhaust existing sources (code, configs, docs, history) before asking. Only ask when options have materially different tradeoffs the user must decide.
- **If multiple choices are acceptable**, pick the most conservative/standard option and proceed; state the choice.
- **Do NOT include an "Other" option** — the UI always offers free-text input alongside your options.
</critical>

tools.name: request_secret
tools.description:
Ask the user for a credential (API key, token, password) that you need and that is not available yet.

<conditions>
- A command or call fails because a credential is missing, or the task clearly requires one
- The secret is NOT already in the "Available secret env vars" list
</conditions>

<instruction>
- Set `name` to the conventional env var name for the service (GITHUB_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, NPM_TOKEN...); the user can adjust it before saving
- Explain in `reason` what you need the credential for — the user sees this text
- After the user saves it, reference it as $NAME in shell commands; the value itself never enters the conversation
</instruction>

<critical>
- NEVER ask the user to paste a secret into the chat as plain text — always use this tool, so the value is stored securely and redacted from the transcript
- NEVER print, echo, or write the secret value after it is saved
- If the user declines, do not immediately retry the same request; find another way or explain the blocker
</critical>

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Generates an image from a text prompt. Requires the imageGeneration slot to be configured (models.slots.imageGeneration in ~/.fah/config.yaml, or useMainConnection: true to opt into the main connection explicitly). Returns a path to the saved image file. Arguments: prompt (required), size (optional, e.g. "1024x1024"), quality (optional), images (optional, list of reference images: sandbox paths, http(s) URLs, or base64 — supported by OpenRouter image endpoints that accept image input).

tools.name: generate_video
tools.description: Generates a video from a text prompt. Requires the videoGeneration slot to be configured (models.slots.videoGeneration in ~/.fah/config.yaml, or useMainConnection: true to opt into the main connection explicitly). Returns a path to the saved MP4 file. Arguments: prompt (required), size (optional, e.g. "1920x1080"), quality (optional), images (optional, list of reference images: sandbox paths, http(s) URLs, or base64 — supported by OpenRouter video endpoints that accept image input).

tools.name: decide
tools.description: Ask a structured decision model (OpenRouter Decisions API, e.g. inception/mercury-decide:free) typed questions about a state and receive calibrated answers as structured JSON: yes-no questions come back with a probability, choice questions with the picked option plus per-option probabilities, score questions with a calibrated score over the ordered legend. Requires the main connection to be an OpenRouter provider. Arguments: model (required), state (required — text or JSON), questions (required — object keyed by question name; each entry is {type: bool|choice|score, instructions, criteria} — bool questions ride the Decisions API's `noul` wire type)

tools.name: task_status
tools.description: Check the status of spawned subagents. Without an id, lists ALL subagents with their current state, token usage, and last activity. With an id, shows that subagent in detail.

tools.name: task_observe
tools.description: Read the recent message history of a subagent. Useful to inspect what a child discovered or decided before following up.

tools.name: task_send
tools.description: Send a follow-up message to a subagent. A running child receives it in its inbox at the next turn boundary; an idle (waiting for input) or completed child is resumed in its SAME session with the message. The resume wait is capped (1.5s): a child that does not respond in time reports the message queued and keeps waking in the background (check task_status). Failed children are continued with task_resume instead. Remote a2a:<name> children cannot be steered or resumed — they have no local session or inbox; follow up with a new task item.

tools.name: task_resume
tools.description: Resume a FAILED subagent, continuing the SAME session: the run appends to the existing JSONL transcript, keeps the same mailbox id and display name, and never mints a cloned "name-2" session. Use this after transient failures (provider quota, network). The resume wait is capped (1.5s): a child that does not confirm in time reports the resume continuing in the background — it is never restarted (check task_status). Steering running/idle/completed children is task_send; respawning a fresh agent is task (the new child links supersedes).

tools.name: task_cancel
tools.description: Abort a running background subagent job by id (see task_status for ids). The child agent is cancelled; already-settled jobs report their state instead.

tools.name: reply
tools.description:
Deliver your explicit answer to the parent agent. Call this when your task output is ready — the text becomes the parent-visible reply. If you never call it, the parent still sees your final message as a completion notice, but an explicit reply is the reliable channel.

REPORT SIZE: per-message budget 8000 chars — you may send one complete reply even when it is larger: the harness auto-spills it (the full text is stored as an agent:// artifact; the parent gets an excerpt + pointer + completeness, and this tool result names the reference). Manual chunking (ordered agent_message parts with report_id + 0-based part_index, more=false on the last, then a final manifest reply carrying report_id + report_parts) is the FALLBACK for when auto-spill is unavailable. See REPORT SIZE CONTRACT in your system prompt. Never probe the output limit.

tools.name: agent_message
tools.description:
Send a message to another agent: a SIBLING subagent id, "main" for the parent orchestrator (for a final answer prefer reply), an absolute mailbox "<sessionId>/main" to reach another Fa instance sharing this session repo, or "name@machine" to reach a session on another machine (delivered through the A2A gateway; the remote machine must be configured under a2a.servers). A session display NAME from agent_directory works too: "goal_builder" or "goal_builder/main" resolve to that session's live mailbox. The recipient sees the message in its inbox on its next turn; completed siblings are resumed. Unknown ids and full queues are rejected.

REPORT SIZE: budget 8000 chars — oversized same-session bodies auto-spill (stored as an agent:// artifact and delivered as a bounded envelope). Manual chunking (ordered report_id + part_index parts) is the FALLBACK for when auto-spill is unavailable. See REPORT SIZE CONTRACT in your system prompt.

tools.name: agent_directory
tools.description: List the agent mailboxes in the messaging fabric that are worth talking to: LIVE mailboxes (registration-backed presence or recent activity), any mailbox holding pending mail, your subagents, and your own address (marked). Each entry shows its session display NAME when known, a short mailbox id, the pending message count, presence ("live" / "busy (run in progress, accepts mail)" / "offline"), the last-activity time for offline entries, and the working directory (home shortened to ~). Declared capabilities render as sub-lines. Stale mailboxes are hidden — pass all: true to list those too (that also shows FULL mailbox ids; the default view truncates them to save tokens). Address a mailbox by its session name via agent_message ("goal_builder", "goal_builder/main", or "name@machine" — a peer on another machine is reachable through the A2A gateway when an a2a.servers entry exists for it); asleep targets are woken with a headless run automatically.

tools.name: task
tools.description:
Your session context is limited. Before performing a user request, think whether the work can be delegated to subagents — orchestrate subagents and deliver the result to the user. If it is a simple ask, just perform it yourself.

Run subagents in parallel by passing multiple items in a single `tasks[]` batch. Execution blocks until every item finishes unless `background` is true — then you receive job ids immediately and results deliver as jobs settle.

# Task Design
- **Agent typing:** Pick each item's `agent` type. Read-only research MUST use `agent: "explore"`. Use the default worker only when no specialist fits.
- **No overhead:** Each `task` MUST instruct its subagent to skip formatters, linters, and project-wide test suites. Run those once at the end.
- **One pass:** Prefer subagents that investigate AND edit in one pass; spin a read-only `explore` only when the affected files are genuinely unknown.

# Inputs
- `context`: Shared project state, constraints, and contracts. Applies to the entire batch; do not duplicate this background into individual tasks.
- `tasks[]`: Array of subagents to spawn.
  - `name`: A stable identifier (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`), used to address the agent (`agent://` urls, job ids). Uniquified per session; generated from the agent type if omitted.
  - `agent`: The agent type running this item. Omitting it gives you the general-purpose worker (`task`) — NEVER pass that name explicitly. Only omit it after checking the agent list below and finding no specialist that fits.
  - `task`: Complete, self-contained instructions. One-liners or missing acceptance criteria are PROHIBITED.
  - `outputSchema`: Invocation-specific JSON Schema. The subagent's final message must then be a JSON document satisfying it; invalid output gets ONE fix retry, then the item fails.
- `background`: Run items as background jobs (default: host configuration). Blocking calls return every item's output in the result.

# Communication
Subagents start blank — no conversation history. Put everything they need into `context` (shared) and `task` (per item). After spawn, the family stays connected:
- `task_send {id, message}`: steer a running child, answer a waiting (idle) one, or RESUME a completed one with follow-up work.
- `task_resume {id, message?}`: continue a FAILED child in its SAME session — same id, same transcript, same mailbox, never a cloned `name-2` session. Use it after transient failures (provider quota, network); `task_send` is for running/idle/completed children, a fresh `task` for a clean restart (the new child links `supersedes`).
- `task_status` / `task_observe`: inspect the family at any time — status, tokens, and the child's recent transcript.
- Children can `reply` (their explicit answer to you) and `agent_message` (sibling↔sibling hand-offs) — a child that finishes without replying surfaces a `completed_without_reply` notice with its final text preview.
- Completed subagents stay addressable: send them more work instead of re-spawning duplicates.
- Remote `a2a:<name>` children cannot be steered, resumed, or observed — they have no local session. Follow up with a new task item against the same `a2a:<name>` agent.

# Waiting is idle, not blocked
- Long-running children (test suites, builds, research): spawn them with `background: true` and END YOUR TURN right after spawning. Completions and inbox mail wake you automatically, and each result arrives as a message — waiting is an idle state, never a blocked turn.
- NEVER park your turn waiting on children (foreground watch loops, blocking re-polls, sleep-style watchers). A parked turn is unreachable: owner messages queue behind it for as long as the wedge lasts.
- If a blocking call is still running when a user message arrives, the call soft-yields to background — do not re-block afterwards; finish the reply and end the turn.

# Format Contracts
`context` format:
# Goal         ← what the batch accomplishes
# Constraints  ← rules and session decisions
# Contract     ← shared interfaces

`task` format:
# Target       ← exact files and symbols; explicit non-goals
# Change       ← step-by-step add/remove/rename; APIs and patterns
# Acceptance   ← observable result; no project-wide commands

# Results
Each item's full output is addressable as `agent://<id>`. An explicit child `reply` is the deliverable — verbatim within the budget, else a bounded `agent://` envelope (excerpt + pointer + completeness); never a silent stub. Resumed children carry their final answer on the completion notice; a reply acked before a kill survives the resume. For items with an `outputSchema`, the stored output IS the validated JSON object, so typed fields are addressable as `agent://<id>/<dot.path>` (e.g. `agent://Explore/findings.0.path`).

# Report Size
A child report above the per-message budget is never silently truncated: the full redacted text is stored as an `agent://` artifact and the result carries a bounded excerpt, the pointer, and explicit completeness (`complete`/`partial`). Resolve the pointer for the whole report. Chunked reports get a final manifest `reply` the harness validates against the observed parts; missing, duplicated, or out-of-order sets are marked INCOMPLETE.

# Available Agents
### task
General-purpose subagent with full capabilities for delegated multi-step tasks
### explore (READ-ONLY)
Read-only codebase research: rapid analysis, pattern searches, and compressed findings for handoff (uses the smol model role when configured)
### review (READ-ONLY)
Read-only code review specialist for quality and security analysis (uses the slow model role when configured)
### plan (READ-ONLY)
Read-only planning specialist that produces implementation plans without editing code

tools.name: checkpoint
tools.description:
Creates a context checkpoint before exploratory work so you can later rewind and keep only a concise report.

Use this when you need to investigate with many intermediate tool calls (read/grep/glob/etc.) and want to minimize context cost afterward.

Rules:
- You MUST call `rewind` before finishing after starting a checkpoint.
- You NEVER call `checkpoint` while another checkpoint is active in the
  same turn. A checkpoint never spans user turns: if one is left unrewound
  when the turn ends, the next `checkpoint` call auto-closes it (the tool
  result names the closed checkpoint) and proceeds.

Typical flow:
1. `checkpoint(goal: …)`
2. Perform exploratory work
3. `rewind(report: …)` with concise findings

After rewind, intermediate checkpoint messages are removed from active context and replaced by the report. The dropped history stays in the session tree; nothing is lost.

tools.name: rewind
tools.description:
End an active checkpoint. Rewind context to it, replacing intermediate exploration with your report.

Call immediately after `checkpoint`-started investigative work.

Requirements:
- `report` MUST be concise, factual, and actionable.
- Include key findings, decisions, and any unresolved risks.
- AVOID raw scratch logs unless essential.
- You MUST call this before finishing if a checkpoint is active.

Behavior:
- If no checkpoint is active, this tool errors. If the checkpoint already rewound, continue from the retained report instead of retrying.
- On success, the session rewinds, keeps your report as retained context, and closes the checkpoint.
- A successful rewind is final for that checkpoint; repeat calls error.

tools.name: compact_expand
tools.description:
Surface and reopen hidden context segments.

Call with NO arguments to list what is hidden: the index of hidden segments with id, kind, size, and a first-line preview each. Pass `query` to filter and rank that index by keyword — it searches the full hidden content, not just previews, so use it when you know WHAT you need but not the id. Discovery is free: it never consumes the expand budget.

To read a segment back, pass its numeric id or range from a marker as `target` (e.g. `5` or `2-6`). Context markers like `[3:hidden·tool_result·4.2k·"first line…"]` or `[2-6:ckpt·38k→40tok·covers:3,5]` are doors, not gravestones: the underlying records stay on disk.

- Giant segments are paged: pass `page` (1-based) to continue past the first page; each page footer states the exact continue call.
- Expanded content counts toward a per-turn budget; every success states the budget left, and when the budget is exhausted the result says so and resets on the next user turn. Only hidden, checkpoint-covered, or summary-folded records expand — the tool tells you when a record is already visible.
- The session file never changes; an expanded segment may be re-hidden later by compaction.

Prefer a targeted expand over re-reading files when the fact was already in context once, and prefer discovery + query over blind ids.

## Managing segments yourself (tier 2)

Pass `action` with a `target` to manage segments directly, without waiting for pressure:

- `action: "hide"` folds a segment you know is dead weight into its expandable marker immediately — one-line marker stays where the content was, `compact_expand` reopens it any time. Real user turns are never hideable; pair groups hide whole; the most recent turns and pinned segments are rejected with the reason.
- `action: "pin"` shields a segment from every hide/compact path (yours, the judge's, pressure-time LRU re-hide); `action: "unpin"` releases it. Pins render on the marker (`·pinned`) and survive session reload.

Hiding and pinning are session state, not edits: the records stay in the file byte-for-byte.

tools.name: session_search
tools.description: Search the WHOLE session archive (every past turn — hidden, compacted and checkpointed regions included), not just the current context. Use it whenever the user references a past decision, rule, task or artifact ("remember when…", "the rules we made") BEFORE answering from assumption. Returns pointers (id, kind, timestamp, preview), never full content — pull the record back with compact_expand. With mode: "map" it reports the archive structure instead: record-kind counts, hidden/checkpoint totals, checkpoint tree with nesting depth.

Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
